drag_tilted.why: tilted 6 deg onto its rear end: the hand lifts 25.6 N and pulls 3.0 N (25.8 N of the 40 N hold) with no torque, but it balances on two points (hand + rear end): it can roll about that line, and only the 4 N m hold torque keeps it upright; one hand at the side of the body

carry2.hands: both on the handlebar, 0.24 m apart
carry2.why: 14.7 N a hand (37 % of the hold's 40 N); the centre of mass is 0.19 m off the bar, 2.9 N m a hand (72 % of the 4.0 N m hold torque; past it the deck swings down until its far end touches the floor, which turns the carry into a drag, not a drop); the robot carries 3.0 kg about 0.52 m ahead of the pelvis (the 0.3 kg basket already pitched the pelvis 0.13 rad, run 1119_001520)

physics.why_recommended: carry2: the load is split evenly between the hands, nothing balances on a point, the hold limits are not reached (force and torque), it is the same take / stand / walk / set down pattern as the toy-basket carry that worked live (run 1118_232318); dragging upright is impossible by physics (13.8 N m needed at the hand), and the tilted drag puts 26 N on ONE hand at the side of the body with a roll the hold must stop
